orig.credit: Attributed to Rabanus Maurus (9th century); Latin text as in the Vatican's edition

stanzas: visit the minds of your own,
fill with grace from on high
You who are called the Paraclete,
finger of the Father's right hand,
Kindle a light for the senses,
May you drive the enemy further off
with you thus going before as guide
Grant that through you we may know the Father
and come to know the Son,
and you, the Spirit of both,
may we believe in at all times.
To God the Father be glory,
and to the Son, who from the dead

notes: line 2.1: 'Paraclete' (Greek parakletos) is the Gospel of John's name for the Spirit: one called to stand by, a helper, advocate or comforter. Kept as a name.
line 3.1: 'septiformis munere', sevenfold in gift: the seven gifts of the Spirit (after Isaiah 11:2-3).
line 3.2: 'finger of the Father's right hand': the Spirit as God's finger (compare Luke 11:20 with Matthew 12:28).
line 3.3: 'promissum Patris', the promise of the Father (Acts 1:4); 'rite' means duly, rightly, as is fitting.
line 3.4: 'sermone ditans guttura', enriching throats with speech: the gift of tongues at Pentecost (Acts 2:4).
lines 4.3-4.4: 'infirma nostri corporis' is literally 'the weak things of our body'; 'virtute perpeti' is 'with perpetual strength'.
lines 6.3-6.4: 'credamus' governs 'te': may we believe you (believe in you), the Spirit of both, at all times.
stanza 7: this doxology names the resurrection ('qui a mortuis surrexit'); other editions close with a different doxology.
